original_motivation: Improve the useful finite captured OFF enclosure budget without spending a 64-core machine on repeated short serial work.
user_instruction: Run lightweight executions in ChatGPT; hand only genuinely heavy, parallel-accelerable calculations to NCP 64 cores / 128 GB RAM.
scope: Same 2440 OFF captured first-two-step paths, fixed binary64-realified gas stages, source switches, species masks, initial data, weights, photon carry and signed energy seams. No mode sum.
exact_zero_nodes: 2345 through 2439 inclusive; retain zero without quadrature
ncp_selection: Choose once from measured local N512/N1024 costs and widths, then seal WORK_PLAN and EXECUTION_LOCK. Do not run both full batches.
protected_kernels: Reuse all three inherited Decimal directed interval kernels byte-for-byte. No binary64/Fortran substitution for the validated Decimal arithmetic lane.
hpc_policy: OpenMPI distributes independent paths, all ranks compute, one thread per rank, exact rational deterministic post-reduction. Local process transport tests the same rank protocol but is not evidence of an actual MPI run. No hidden backend fallback.
acceptance: All input and source identities verified against actual saved bytes
Actual bounded local science and precision/resolution controls completed
Raw old/new weighted endpoints compared for all 34 metrics without intersection
Direct retained sums reproduce all predecessor full intervals exactly
Independent reviewer evaluates scoped admission and ready-for-heavy-batch delivery
Self-contained backup contains all runtime inputs, code, local completed evidence and handoff
forbidden: automatically retry a failed heavy path
authorization: Current research-loop request and inherited additive draft-PR and Drive/Dropbox backup authorization; no additional attachment required.
failure_policy: Preserve first failure and partial evidence. Fix concrete in-scope defects with affected validation. No unchanged blind retry. Execution, numerical acceptance, independent admission and publication are separate.
